question:
A 37-year-old male presents to the clinic complaining of throbbing pain at the base of his skull since
last night. He was mopping his kitchen when he slipped backward, hitting his head on the floor. He
denies loss of consciousness and review of systems is otherwise negative. He has no significant past
medical history and takes no medications. Vital signs reveal: | Temperature | 36.7°C (98.1°F) | | --- | --- |
| Blood pressure | 124/78 mm Hg | | Heart rate | 82/min | | Respiratory rate | 14/min | On examination,
the patient is in mild discomfort but is appropriately alert and oriented. A complete neurological exam is
unremarkable. There is a 2 cm superficial laceration within a well-circumscribed area of erythema,
edema, and ecchymosis at the base of the skull. The cranial rhythmic impulse (CRI) is about 6 cycles
per minute, and there is a moderate decrease in the amplitude of the components of its cycles. Which
of the following would be an expected additional finding in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Increased
amplitude of the cranial rhythmic impulse (CRI) (B) Unilateral sacral flexion (C) Torsion of the sacrum

around an oblique axis (D) Decreased sacral nutation (E) Decreased amplitude of the occipital motion
during cranial flexion (F) Bilateral sacral flexion (G) Bilateral sacral extension (H) Compression of the
sphenobasilar synchondrosis (I) Increased sacral nutation (J) Unilateral sacral extension
 A. Unilateral sacral flexion
B. Increased sacral nutation
C. Torsion of the sacrum around an oblique axis
D. Decreased sacral nutation
E. Bilateral sacral extension
F. Increased amplitude of the cranial rhythmic impulse (CRI)
G. Bilateral sacral flexion
H. Unilateral sacral extension
I. Decreased amplitude of the occipital motion during cranial flexion
J. Compression of the sphenobasilar synchondrosis
